gv._readme: Identity merges for the GV base (PRO-75): each canonical keeps the live site's own rendering; duplicates are pre-rename archive rows, the firm's own misspellings and one EDGAR issuer renamed by a reverse merger. Written 2026-09-29 before the first prepare.

merges.name: Warp

merges.name: Tend

merges.name: Waltz Health
merges.reason: one company: Asset Blue Pharmacy Services, Inc. is Waltz Health's legal entity (its 2022 Form D names Mark Thierer, Waltz Health's CEO, as executive officer and Benjamin Robbins as director from Google's Cambridge office, 355 Main Street)

merges.name: Apteligent
merges.reason: one company: Crittercism renamed Apteligent (2015), acquired by VMware (2017); the firm listed both names

merges.name: BBOT
merges.reason: one company: BridgeBio Oncology Therapeutics does business as BBOT (the firm listed the full name in 2024-25, BBOT from 2025)

merges.name: nChroma Bio
merges.reason: one lineage: Chroma Medicine (GV's list 2023-24, Issi Rozen) and Nvelop Therapeutics (GV's list 2024, David Schenkein) merged as nChroma Bio in December 2024 (GV's live list, Issi Rozen); two GV positions became one company, so one row carries the earliest entry

merges.name: Allara Health
merges.reason: one company: Astrid Health Inc. (Form D 0001990492-23-000001, Frederique Dame a director, New York, 2023) is Allara's legal entity (judge j2); it is not Astrid, the to-do app (never_merge astrid/astrid-health-inc)

merges.name: Vera Therapeutics
merges.reason: one company: TruCode Gene Repair (GV's 2019 listing) renamed Vera Therapeutics in April 2020 (judge j14)

merges.name: Redpanda
merges.reason: one company: Vectorized (vectorized.io, GV's 2021 listing) renamed Redpanda Data in 2021; the firm lists Redpanda from 2022 (judges j14, j17)

merges.name: Omni
merges.reason: one company: the firm's live list carries Omni Analytics twice, as 'Omni Analytics' (exploreomni.com, Crystal Huang) and 'Omni' (omni.co, its current domain); the /ai list dates both to April 2022 (judges j9, j17); slug omni as in first-round-capital, redpoint-ventures and iconiq-growth

merges.name: myLaurel
merges.reason: one company: Ready Responders (readyresponders.com, GV's 2020-23 listing) operates as myLaurel; readyresponders.com serves myLaurel's site, the firm replaced Ready with myLaurel in 2023 under the same partner, and myLaurel's 2025 round names GV as a previous investor (judge j17)

merges.name: Backplane
merges.reason: one company: Place (place.xyz, GV's 2015-16 listing) is the product Backplane pivoted to in 2015, under the same partner (David Krane); Backplane sold its assets in April 2016 (Global Venturing 2016-04-15; judge j17)

merges.name: Hired
merges.reason: one company: DeveloperAuction rebranded as Hired.com in September 2013 (TechCrunch 2013-09-17; judge j16)

merges.name: DJZ
merges.reason: one company: Crossfader (crossfader.fm, GV's 2015-17 listing) is the DJ app built by Seth Goldstein's DJZ team (TechCrunch 2014-06-27; judge j16)

merges.name: Beamable
merges.reason: one company: Disruptor Beam relaunched as Beamable in 2020 (GamesIndustry.biz 2020-04-22); both rows resolve to one SEC registrant (CIK 1579283)

merges.name: DailyCred
merges.reason: one company: DailyCred was 'born as Shopobot' (the company's own farewell page, which calls Google Ventures 'our first major investor'); Shopobot's June 2011 seed is the same round both rows cite (TechCrunch 2011-06-16); the firm listed both names in 2013 during the pivot (judge d2)

merges.name: Voltron Data
merges.reason: one lineage (decisions R2): Ursa Computing, whose $4.9M seed GV led in October 2020, folded into Voltron Data in 2021 ('Ursa Labs is now Voltron Data Labs'; Voltron's 2022 launch names Ursa's leadership among its founders); GV then joined Voltron's seed and Series A. One row, entry read through Voltron's own seed, Ursa's seed recorded in the note (judge d5)

merges.name: Rockbot
merges.reason: one company: Roqbot (the recall addition, 2012 seed led by Google Ventures and Detroit Venture Partners) renamed itself Rockbot, the name the firm lists from 2013 (same CEO Garrett Dodge, same start at Bar Basic; TechCrunch 2014 and 2015; judge d1)

merges.name: Carnival Mobile
merges.reason: one company: Carnival Labs (carnivallabs.com, the firm's 2013-14 listing) is Carnival Mobile (carnivalmobile.com, then carnival.io, 2014 on), the New Zealand-founded mobile-messaging company Sailthru bought in 2016; both rows cite the same 2013 $2.4M round (sweep judge s1)

merges.name: Teem
merges.reason: one company: EventBoard (eventboard.io, the firm's 2014-16 listing) renamed itself Teem ('Teem started its operating life as Eventboard', Sixteen:Nine 2018-09-14), which WeWork bought in 2018 (sweep judge s1)

merges.name: MixBit
merges.reason: one company: in 2014 AVOS Systems sold Delicious and turned into a single company working only on MixBit (TechCrunch 2014-06-06); the firm listed AVOS 2012-14 and MixBit 2014-19 under the same partner, David Krane (sweep judge s1)

merges.name: Fabric
merges.reason: one company: Florence (florenceos.com, the firm's 2023 listing) renamed itself Fabric in 2024 ('Florence becomes Fabric', fabrichealth.com/about); same partner, Sangeen Zeb

merges.name: Jetify
merges.reason: one company: 'Jetify Inc., formerly Jetpack Technologies Inc.' (jetpack.io); the firm listed Jetpack Technologies 2023-25 and Jetify from 2025 under the same partner, Erik Nordlander

merges.name: Simply
merges.reason: one company: JoyTunes renamed itself Simply in 2022 (Wikipedia); the firm listed JoyTunes 2021-23 and Simply from 2022 under the same partner, Tom Hulme

merges.name: Crews by Core
merges.reason: one company: Core (bycore.com, Di-Ann Eisnor's construction-labor company, the firm's 2020-26 archive listing) renamed itself Crews by Core and was bought by WakeCap in 2024 (Business Insider 2024-07-02); the live list carries Crews by Core

merges.name: Collaborate
merges.reason: one company: Kibits Corp. became Collaborate.com (the 2013 collaborate.com pages read '© 2013 Kibits Corp.'; kibits.com forwarded there), which Cisco bought in December 2013 (Cisco's S-8 of 2014-01-07 assumes the Kibits Corp. equity plan; sweep judge s3)

merges.name: LaunchKit
merges.reason: one company: the Cluster team pivoted the company to LaunchKit ('$1.6 million for Cluster and an additional $600,000 after it decided to focus on LaunchKit', TechCrunch 2016-07-27), then joined Google and open-sourced LaunchKit; the Cluster app runs on under its makers' separate small company, Fotoloce (sweep judge s3)

never_merge.reason: two companies: Miso (gomiso.com, a social TV check-in app) and Miso Media (misomedia.com, a music-learning app)
two companies: Secret (secret.ly, the 2014 anonymous-sharing app, MG Siegler) and Secret Escapes (secretescapes.com, the London travel company, Tom Hulme); the builder's word-prefix rule folded them
two companies: Astrid (astrid.com, the to-do app Yahoo bought in 2013) and Astrid Health Inc. (New York, a 2023 Form D with Frederique Dame as director)
two companies: Bloom (bloomcloser.com, an elder-care device, 2015-17 listings, Rich Miner) and Bloom Institute of Technology (Lambda School)
two companies: Spruce (sprucehealth.com, the dermatology and care-communication app later listed as Spruce Health) and Spruce Finance (residential solar financing, now Spruce Power)
two companies: Spruce Health (sprucehealth.com) and Spruce Finance (sprucefinance.com, now sprucepower.com)

two companies: Bowery (bowery.io, developer environments, MG Siegler, the firm's 2014-15 listings) and Bowery Farming (boweryfarming.com, the 2017-24 listings); the builder's name-variant rule folded the split back (judge j2, recall triage)
two companies: Basis (basis.io, the 2018 algorithmic stablecoin, shut December 2018, the firm's 2018-19 listings) and Basis (getbasis.ai, AI agents for accounting firms, the firm's 2026 listing)
